title: The mechanisms of muscle hypertrophy and their application to resistance training
summary: Reviews the three primary drivers of muscle growth: mechanical tension, muscle damage, and metabolic stress.
relevance: Explains why progressively loaded resistance exercise builds muscle size.

title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
summary: Higher weekly set volumes produced greater gains in muscle mass, with a graded dose-response.
relevance: Supports accumulating enough weekly sets per muscle when programming for hypertrophy.

title: Strength and hypertrophy adaptations between low- vs. high-load resistance training: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
summary: Both light and heavy loads grow muscle similarly when sets are taken near failure; heavier loads favour maximal strength.
relevance: Lets trainees choose loads that fit the goal — strength or hypertrophy — with either working for size.

title: Effectiveness of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and continuous endurance training for VO2max improvements: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Milanović Z, Sporiš G, Weston M
summary: HIIT and moderate continuous training both raise VO2max, with HIIT producing slightly larger improvements.
relevance: Backs interval and steady-state cardio as effective ways to build aerobic capacity.

title: What is best practice for training intensity and duration distribution in endurance athletes?
summary: Describes polarized training — a large base of low-intensity work with smaller amounts of high-intensity effort.
relevance: Frames why easy-paced aerobic (zone 2) work forms the backbone of endurance development.

title: Effects of resistance exercise on bone health
summary: Reviews evidence that mechanical loading from resistance exercise stimulates bone formation and preserves bone mineral density.
relevance: Explains why loaded, weight-bearing movements support skeletal health and bone density.

title: Effects of diaphragmatic breathing on health: a narrative review
summary: Slow diaphragmatic breathing is associated with improved autonomic balance, reduced stress, and better respiratory function.
relevance: Supports dedicated breath-work drills that train the diaphragm and respiratory control.
